holdings.thesis: HOLD: shares ~$437, up from last week's $412-$430 range -- Lake Street/Freedom Broker/Goldman Buy ratings from earlier this week remain the operative bull case, no new negative data today. Still down -29.0% vs. cost basis on stop-loss review (legacy of original entry price), but position stays small (3.3% of portfolio) after two prior trims and price strength argues against a further cut.

HOLD: shares ~$168, roughly flat since last review. BofA trimmed its PT to $275 (from $340) on 9/1 but maintained Buy; this is already reflected in the three prior trims from the guidance-miss selloff. FY27 guidance still implies 85%+ revenue growth and 18 of 18 covering analysts rate it Buy -- no new negative data, holding the de-risked (5.4%) remainder.

HOLD: thesis intact and strengthening -- shares ~$146, still carrying most of the gains from Evercore's 9/1 Outperform/$210 upgrade (Mahaney's 'Netflix-like' comeback thesis) and DA Davidson's $175 PT. The earnings-decline flag remains attributable to AI-feature reinvestment rather than demand softness. Position eased to 14.1% of portfolio (from 14.9%), back under the cap with room, no forced trim needed today.

HOLD: shares ~$56.12, roughly flat. No new insider filings or negative data since the 9/4 Form 4 (Forlenza's 10,000-share sale) already reflected in the two prior trims (~85% combined reduction); position is already minimal (1.4% of portfolio) so no further trim is warranted. CEO succession (Singhal to CEO effective 9/30) remains known and unchanged; Q2 fundamentals (58% revenue growth, reaffirmed 40%+ FY guidance) still support holding the remainder.

HOLD: shares continued higher to ~$290.83 (from ~$280.53), extending the reaction to the UtilityInnovation acquisition (~$1.45B cash, up to $1.15B EBITDA-linked earnouts) announced this week; ex-date for the $0.062 quarterly dividend is 9/14. The Hagens Berman/Pomerantz securities-fraud investigations remain a known, unchanged overhang. Position at 13.8% of portfolio, under the 15% cap -- no action needed.

HOLD: thesis intact -- shares ~$338, essentially flat since the 9/7 review. The antitrust win on the ad-exchange divestiture and Gemini 3.8 Flash rollout remain the known positive drivers; market attention today is on balancing Alphabet's cloud/AI growth against elevated capex, not company-specific negative news. No new catalyst either way.

HOLD: shares ~$257, little changed. Amazon confirmed it is cooperating with NTSB investigators on Saturday's fatal Amazon Air cargo crash in Miami -- a reputational/operational item to monitor but not yet a fundamentals-affecting data point. The FTC/22-state ad-pricing lawsuit remains the known overhang; Q2 fundamentals (AWS +36.7% YoY, operating income +43%) still support the thesis, 59 of 59 analysts rate Buy.

HOLD: modest positive -- shares +1.0% to ~$161 after subsidiary Pioneer Natural Resources launched tender offers on $2.1B of outstanding senior notes (pricing 9/14), a routine balance-sheet management move. Piper Sandler's $185 PT (9/3) and the $1.03/share Q3 dividend (payable 9/10) remain the known drivers. Thesis intact, no action needed.

HOLD: thesis intact -- BofA raised its PT to $93 (from $88, Buy maintained), continuing the wave of post-earnings target hikes (Truist $85, Goldman $115, Bernstein $110). CEO Levchin's fireside chat at Goldman's Communacopia + Technology Conference is today (9/8, 3:05pm PT) -- watching for commentary but no results yet; no new negative data.

HOLD: mixed but not thesis-breaking -- shares ~$210, still digesting the 9/5 insider-selling headlines (grouped with PDD/Roblox/TI/Fastly) already reflected in the prior review; position remains small (3.7% of portfolio). Q2 revenue +36% YoY and raised FY26 guidance are the fundamental anchor; the known OpenAI spend-deceleration flag remains the primary driver of the post-earnings pullback, not fresh deterioration.

HOLD: shares down ~2% to ~$1,124 today, but the move tracks a broader healthcare/biotech risk-off session (sector -1.7%) driven by unrelated Phase 3 trial failures at other companies (Novartis), not an Eli Lilly-specific data point. The GLP-1 franchise, pending $2.88B Merida Biosciences acquisition, and Buy consensus ($1,302.60 PT, 24 of 26 analysts) remain intact; presents at Morgan Stanley's healthcare conference 9/14.

HOLD: thesis intact -- shares ~$18, roughly flat. The Notre Dame partnership and Kraken stablecoin deal, plus this week's Scotiabank/Piper Sandler initiations, remain the known supportive data points. CEO Noto's fireside chat at Goldman's Communacopia conference is today (9/8) -- watching for credit-quality/growth commentary but no results yet.

HOLD: thesis intact -- shares ~$822, extending the past year's 95% run on record $20.5B Q2 revenue (+24% YoY) and a $72B backlog. Bernstein's 9/3 Hold rating and CEO Creed's 9/1 insider sale are known, already-reviewed data points; analysts continue raising earnings estimates while flagging valuation risk, but no new negative catalyst today.

HOLD: thesis strengthening -- today's Investor Day delivered the expected catalyst: FY26 revenue guidance raised to $450-460M (from prior guidance) following the SkyWater acquisition close, and shares rose to ~$40.47. 44 of 52 analysts rate Buy with a median PT of $65 (~60% upside). Position stays modest (2.4% of portfolio) given the company's pre-profit risk profile; no trim warranted on a positive catalyst day.
